In the 1960s, the CIA turned a cat into a spy.
The idea was simple. Cats can wander anywhere, and nobody suspects a cat.
So surgeons put a microphone in its ear, a transmitter at the base of its skull, and an antenna along its tail.
They called it Operation Acoustic Kitty.
But there was a problem. Whenever the cat got hungry, it wandered off to find food.
So, reportedly, they operated again, to stop it feeling hungry.
The whole project is said to have cost around twenty million dollars.
Finally, the first real mission. Listen in on two men on a park bench, near the Soviet embassy.
They let the cat out of a van. It walked across the street.
And was hit by a taxi.
At least, that's how one former CIA officer told it. Others say the cat lived, and the equipment was simply removed.
Either way, a secret memo concluded that spy cats were not practical.
